howDoI.q: How do I make a leaf that turns over as it falls?
How do I make a leaf float down instead of dropping?
How do I make a tree drop leaves by itself?
How do I make a gust that bends every tree at once?
How do I make a leaf lie on the grass after it lands?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Leaves in the Wind is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about leaves falling from autumn trees. A leaf is a monster: a few pictures that turn it over as it goes, and a path that carries it down. A tree is a set of blocks, and a branch is a block that gives birth to a leaf every few seconds. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages here, the How this level is made page of each level in particular. Related Starters: Gusts has wind that pushes the hero, Twinkle, Twinkle shows why every cell of one block keeps the same clock, and Beams and Fog moves fog with monsters.

pages.head: Level 1: The Tumble
pages.html:
Level 1: The Tumble

Three maples stand in a row, each with a sign. A branch on each tree drops a leaf every few seconds, all three at the same moment, so they can be watched side by side.

The first leaf is one picture going straight down: it looks like a red stone. The second has eight frames that spin it and turn it over, but it still goes straight down, and it still looks like a stone, only a spinning one. The third rocks to and fro, now and then tumbles, and swoops from side to side on a zigzag path, slow at the end of each swing. That one floats.

Stand by each tree and watch a leaf all the way down. The door at the end leads on to the wind.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the tumble is made

  • A leaf is a monster. Open leaves.mon in the monsters editor. Every leaf has Power 150, so touching Mara does nothing to it, and its pictures take no hit points. Its Lives is Until the end of its path: when it reaches the grass it is destroyed, and When destroyed it becomes a leaf lying on the grass.
  • A branch gives birth. In tumble.bbl each tree's middle-right block, branch0 to branch2, has a monster to give birth to and 100 ticks between births (there are 18.2 ticks in a second). The three keep the same time, so their leaves let go together.
  • Eight frames. leaves.mbl has each kind of leaf drawn eight times, maple.0 to maple.7. From one frame to the next the leaf spins an eighth of a turn and turns over an eighth of the way, so in the middle it is seen edge on, a thin line, and then from its paler back. Each half of the leaf is folded up a little at the vein, so one half is in the light and the other in shade.
  • The stiff leaf shows only maple.0, and its path is one corner: five blocks down at speed 2.
  • The spinning leaf shows the eight frames in turn, 2 or 3 ticks each, on the same path. Turning is not enough.
  • The floating leaf rocks between maple.7, maple.0 and maple.1 for a while, then tumbles through all eight: sixteen pictures in its list, for 3 to 6 ticks each. Its path has nine corners: a swoop two blocks across and one down at speed 2, a glide one block across at speed 1, a swoop back, a glide back, and so on. The corners going left are flipped (their facing is mirrored), so the leaf tips the way it swings.
  • The path does not know about the frames. They run on their own times. Because the two go round at different speeds, the leaf never looks quite the same twice on its way down.

pages.head: Level 2: The Gust
pages.html:
Level 2: The Gust

A meadow with three trees: a red maple with big pointed leaves, an orange oak with long round-lobed ones and a yellow birch with small ones shaped like a drop, on a white trunk. Each tree drops leaves of its own kind now and then, and each leaf flutters and drifts a little to the right on a light breeze.

Every nine seconds or so a gust comes. All three crowns bend to the right together, and a handful of leaves tear off every tree at once and fly far to the right, tumbling fast, some lifted up before they come down. A leaf that lands lies on the grass for a few seconds and is gone.

Walk past each tree and wait for a gust. The last door ends the game.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the gust is made

  • Three kinds of leaf. Each kind has its own shape, size and colors, and its own eight frames, and each has a picture of itself lying on the grass: maple.rest, oak.rest and birch.rest. The leaf that lies there has Lives For a set time, 55 ticks, and no path.
  • Calm leaves. The two bottom corners of each crown are branches, each with its own time between births: 83 and 117 ticks on the maple, 97 and 131 on the oak, 73 and 109 on the birch. No two keep the same time, so the leaves fall at moments that seem to have no pattern.
  • The gust is one loop. Each top block of every crown is a loop of five blocks: leaning hard for 16 ticks, upright for 78, a little lean for 8, upright for 64, and a little lean for 4, then round again (170 ticks in all). The game keeps one clock for each block number, and all nine loops keep the same times, so all three trees bend in the same tick.
  • The leaves let go with it. The last block of each loop, the little lean, gives birth to a gust leaf every 170 ticks. A block only gives birth while it is the one showing, and that last block is showing just as each 170 ticks come round, so three leaves leave each tree at once, just before the crowns lean hard.
  • Where the paths came from. The paths were worked out by a little wind model in the game's build script: gravity pulls the leaf down, drag keeps its speed close to the air's, a sway swings it from side to side (gliding, it falls slowly; at each turn it rises a little), and a breeze to the right rises and falls by itself. For a gust leaf the model picks a moment when the wind is strong. Then each flight was cut to at most ten corners in whole blocks, each with the speed that keeps its timing.
  • Not too many. A block only gives birth while it is near the screen, and every leaf is gone a few seconds after it lands, so there are never more than about twenty leaves at once. The game draws up to 50 monsters on the screen.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It has no wind and no random. Nothing pushes a monster. Every leaf follows the path it was given, from the same place, the same way, every time. The wind is in the paths, worked out before the game was made. Many leaves with different paths and different times are what make it feel windy.
  • A path is ten corners, in whole blocks. A leaf cannot swing less than a block, and it moves in straight lines between corners. Its speed is a whole number of pixels a tick, so a slow glide is 1 and a swoop is 2.
  • Frames do not follow the path. A leaf's pictures go round on their own times. The only link between the two is the facing of each corner, which can flip the picture.
  • Mara cannot make a gust. A monster's path cannot change because the hero walks or touches it. Kicking leaves up would take a monster that attacks: one that follows a second path when the hero comes near.
  • One clock per block. To bend the trees in the same tick, their top blocks keep the same times. To keep the calm leaves out of step, every branch needs its own block.
  • Blocks are not free. A block set holds 150 blocks. The gust loops here cost 45 of them, and the signs 40.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Give the stiff leaf in level 1 the floating leaf's path, and see how much of the floating comes from the path alone.
  • Change the floating leaf's glides from speed 1 to speed 2. It stops floating and starts zigzagging.
  • In gust.bbl, change one tree's top blocks to times of their own. That tree now bends out of step with the others.
  • Change the time between births on the birch's branches to 20 ticks, and watch it shed every leaf it has.
  • Draw a fourth kind of leaf, eight frames of it, and a tree to drop it.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
